calls.body: The Sabres are around the middle of the league for preventing dangerous shots, and the Canadiens are one of the worst. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Caufield wins it in overtime
paras: Josh Norris got the scoring started for the Sabres midway through the first. Zachary Bolduc and Cole Caufield scored a little over two minutes apart later in the period to turn a 1-0 deficit into a 2-1 lead. Alexandre Texier made it 3-1 early in the second, but Jack Quinn cut Montréal’s lead to 3-2 shorthanded a little over two minutes later. Tage Thompson tied it 3-3 midway through the third. Caufield won it with his second goal of the night 54 seconds into overtime.
Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. Jacob Fowler made 23 saves for the Canadiens, and Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen stopped 30 of 34 at the other end.
The Canadiens killed all four Sabres power plays. The Habs moved to 4-3-1 and climbed to sixth in the Atlantic, while the Sabres dropped to 4-3-2, fifth in the Atlantic.

items.text: Tage Thompson passed Jason Pominville for tenth on the Sabres’ all-time goals list, with 218.
Nick Suzuki extended his point streak against Buffalo to ten games.
Alexandre Texier scored his first goal of the season, his first since Mar 11 (18 games played since).
The Sabres were without Rasmus Dahlin, Conor Timmins, Alex Lyon and others. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Wild were missing more at the time.
